description: §7.6 rule (b) (S482 r1) — `${ out = run(g); }` hands `g` to `run`, which calls it, and `g` reads `k`, whose `${ }` comes later in the program body. A function value body code hands on counts as called (§6.7.4 rule 3), so this reaches `k` before its place: E-SCOPE-001. Before #2053 r1 it compiled and showed `k` = 1 (run before the body), not the source-order 5.
rationale: §7.6 rule (b) (S482): "A display … or a body-top statement … that reaches a file-scope binding whose place in the run comes after it — directly, or through a function it calls, at any depth — SHALL be E-SCOPE-001"; S482 r1: "A function value that body code names or writes … counts as if it were called where it stands, as §6.7.4 rule 3 counts one". ruling:user-voice-scrml.md-S481-run-order-followups item 2 — "A display or statement that calls a function reaching a binding whose place is later … E-SCOPE-001" (PA reading of "calls", prov=pa-ruled S482 r1).
